events.text:
IDF fears unilateral attack on Iran could trigger multi-front war
Israeli Military Intelligence has reportedly rejected Prime Minister Netanyahu and Mossad chief Gofman’s assessment that Israel could launch a ‘limited’ 3-5 day operation against Iran and get away with it without any repercussions.
Instead, a new escalation could spark a regional war pulling in Lebanon, Syria and Gaza, Israel’s Channel 12 reports, citing a closed-door security cabinet meeting at which the IDF’s intelligence service made its position clear to Netanyahu and top defense officials.
Separately on Sunday, a source told Israel’s Kan broadcaster that Netanyahu continues[ to lobby President Trump to hit Iran “as soon as possible”](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/78112) despite reported reluctance on Trump’s part.
Iranian officials, military and IRGC leaders have said they’re prepared for any escalation, and indicated that a resumption of full-scale fighting could mean Iranian attacks on previously not-targeted infrastructure like [internet data cables](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77405) and Big Tech interests, and may even expand the conflict beyond the borders of the Middle East.

events.text:
⚔️ Houthis show off massive haul of weapons, equipment left behind by retreating enemy troops
 
Dozens of shipping containers and fortified mountain dugouts packed with pallets of sealed, brand new military equipment, from rifles, mortars, anti-tank weapons and heavy rocket artillery rounds to drones and vehicles still wrapped in factory packaging were displayed in new Ansar Allah photos and footage published Sunday.
The media, shot at military camps outside Mokha, also shows an array of used equipment, from construction vehicles and fuel trucks to pickups, tanks, heavy towed artillery and anti-aircraft guns.
The media is littered with references to Saudi Arabia, including a Royal Saudi Land Forces patch, IDs and shipping manifests. A Pakistan-issued Covid vax certificate was also found, potentially corroborating the Houthi-aligned Yemeni Armed Forces’ recent claims that they captured dozens of Pakistani mercenaries during the Battle of Bab al-Mandab.
Ansar Allah took the entire southwest Yemeni coast in September in a surprise blitz offensive, and expanded their gains last week, driving enemy forces back to within 80 km of Aden, [the enemy capital](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77734).
